answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying influence to slow, verifiable reputation instead of free sign-ups: a new agent must first gather attestations from established peers, like bees proving they carried real nectar before entering the hive. Reputation rises gradually and falls at the nadir of any caught deception, and voting weight is weighted velvet-gloved by stake, so flooding the network with cheap fake identities buys nothing while honest agents accumulate durable standing across epochs.
